rule.summary: one REV ticket per session from the FIXED FTN Month 9 kernel at 9bed235, evaluated on bar-derived DayContext (BID chart, ASK series attached for spread_measured) at every 15m close inside the killzone; direction from the raid; stop beyond the raid's own extreme plus the instrument buffer; minimum stop distance enforced
rule.kernel: ftn.research.kernel_log.session_ticket_log(..., book=None) with config interpretation_triggers all false (ftn/config.yaml as pinned) -> ftn.os.candidates.evaluate_candidates; first selection in the session is the ticket. DayContext from ftn.research.daycontext.History(bid, days, ask=ask, calendar=True)
rule.sessions: London killzone 02:00-05:00 and NY AM killzone 07:00-10:00, America/New_York wall clock; kernel evaluated at each 15m close from start+15m to end inclusive, using only bars up to that close
rule.direction: REV: high raided -> bearish (short), low raided -> bullish (long); both or neither raided -> no ticket (ftn.models.rev.rev_direction)
rule.entry: close of the 15m bar on which the kernel first selects REV
rule.stop: bearish: raid_extreme_high + buffer, buffer = max(1 pt, max(spread_measured, assumed spread) + stop slippage) (US100 assumed spread 1.55 + 0.50 -> >= 2.05 pt; US500 0.72 + 0.25 -> >= 1.0 pt); bullish: raid_extreme_low - max(1 pt, stop slippage) (= 1 pt for both). raid_extreme as in H015b (15m bars from the raid bar to the entry bar). spread_measured = ASK close - BID close at the signal time. ftn.os.instruments.rev_stop_buffer; ftn.os.mint_draft REV _stop
rule.target_and_exit: fixed 2R from the signal entry (BID close); else time exit at the last 1m close before 16:00 NY; stop first on an ambiguous bar. Fills per costs.binding (correct side)
rule.tradeable: every research-draft gate passes except allowlist and the I0 contract gate (ftn.research.kernel_log.tradeable); D18 direction gate, stop-side risk gate and the min-stop gate active; the risk gate sees a FLAT book (kernel_log.FLAT_BOOK) in the binding stream
rule.context_history: the kernel needs >= 22 prior sessions of 1m bars as context; context bars may come from before the counting window (never counted)
rule.min_stop: risk gate blocks a ticket whose |entry - stop| < min_risk = 4 x (assumed spread + 2 x stop/market slippage): US100 10.2 pt, US500 4.88 pt (risk:stop_below_min_risk). A blocked ticket is NOT a trade and is not counted (ex-ante rule, not outcome-dependent); blocks are counted and reported
rule.month8_units: Month-8 measurements in instrument units (1 pip = 1 index point); index CBDR/Asian thresholds = ICT FX thresholds x (median daily range / EURUSD median daily range): US100 x6.743 (CBDR ideal < 269.7, wide >= 337.2), US500 x1.218
rule.calendar: FOMC/CPI/NFP schedule (ftn/src/ftn/research/data/us_macro_events.csv, pinned) is attached as context. The Month 9 kernel does not read it (ftn.research.events docstring); checked at 9bed235 on the burned tape (2026-10-04): calendar on vs --no-calendar gives identical trades (date, killzone, direction, entry, stop, R; US100 146/146, US500 112/112), only the fingerprint, calendar and m8_london_gate log columns differ; the harness must repeat this assertion. The pinned file has CPI/NFP only to 2026-12 and FOMC to 2027-12; it is never extended in the binding run (FTN_EVENTS_CSV override forbidden); an extended DATA-certified calendar may be used only in a separate co-report run
rule.entry_minute: BINDING (CASSANDRA F1): the kernel's entry price is BID.close_at(t) and spread_measured is ASK.close_at(t) - entry, both 'last bar strictly before t' (ftn.research.bars.Series.close_at), and simulate_both fills the entry at ask.c[ask.idx(t)-1] / bid.c[bid.idx(t)-1]. A ticket therefore counts only if a BID bar AND an ASK bar exist with timestamp EXACTLY t - 1 minute; otherwise the row status is feed_gap_entry (not counted, reported with counts). Evaluated for every ticket before any outcome is computed. Burned example: 2026-03-23 US100 ny_am, BID and ASK missing 07:06-07:17 NY, the 07:15 long entered at the stale 07:05 close: phantom +1.984R
rule.no_r_tickets: a tradeable ticket whose binding outcome is R=None (no_entry_bar, no_bars, invalid_stop) is NOT counted; status no_r_ticket, reported with counts by reason

costs.binding: correct-side fills, ftn.research.outcomes.simulate_both(slip_mult=1.0): long enters on ASK close + market slip, stopped when BID low <= stop (fill min(stop, BID open) - stop slip), target when BID high > target (fill target - limit slip); short enters on BID close - market slip, stopped when ASK high >= stop (fill max(stop, ASK open) + stop slip), target when ASK low < target (fill target + limit slip). R = (exit fill - entry fill) / planned risk |signal entry - stop|
costs.spread: per-minute MEASURED Dukascopy ASK - BID (correct-side fills on the ASK series as H016b). The pinned assumed spreads (US100 1.55, US500 0.72) enter only the rule's stop buffer max(spread_measured, assumed) and the min-stop gate, exactly as pinned
co_reports: flat cost 0.8 / 0.5 pt per side (ftn.research.outcomes.simulate; H013/H014/H015b convention) - co-report ONLY (CASSANDRA)
measured spread at the signal (monthly median / p90 per instrument and killzone)
DATA era p90 and p99 spread schedule from procedure S (A5 rule 4 sensitivity)

statistical_test.binding_bound: session-cluster percentile bootstrap. Clusters = (date, killzone) over counted trades pooled across US100 and US500, in canonical order (date, london before ny_am). rng = random.Random(20261004); 10,000 resamples; each resample draws k clusters with rng.randrange(k) (k = number of clusters) and computes sum(R)/count(trades). Sorted values v[0..9999]. Binding one-sided 95% lower bound = v[int(0.05*10000)] = v[500] (the 5th percentile; alpha = 0.05 one-sided). PASS needs v[500] > 0
statistical_test.p_value: one-sided p = (#{v <= 0} + 1) / 10,001 from the same cluster bootstrap
statistical_test.binding_call: harness-implemented session-cluster percentile bootstrap (NOT ftn.research.stats.boot_ci): rng = random.Random(20261004); B = 10,000; v sorted; LB = v[int(0.05*B)] = v[500]; alpha = 0.05 one-sided; p = (#{v <= 0} + 1) / (B + 1)
statistical_test.seed_note: seed 20261004, B = 10,000, index 500 as H016b (no seed choice after data)

expected_N.why_adjusted: min_risk (US100 10.2 pt, US500 4.88 pt), the stop buffer and the slippage floors are pinned in POINTS. Index levels in 2019-2022 were ~1/3-1/2 of the burned window (NDX ~8-15k vs US100 ~25.8k; SPX ~2.9-5.8k vs ~6.9k), so stop distances in points shrink and more tickets fall under the min-stop gate. The central estimate scales each burned ticket's risk_pts by (approximate public annual-average index level / burned median entry) and keeps it iff >= min_risk; vol factors 1.25 / 1.5 allow for higher point volatility (2020, 2022). Levels are general public knowledge, NOT read from the library

orion_rulings.6:
Yes, in either direction, but only if all of these hold:
- Identical frozen rules: same REV version, entry and exit logic, and cost model, including the correct-side co-report.
- No overlapping bars or sessions with H016b's counted window. DATA must certify H017's tape as untouched.
- H017 is pre-registered, with its tag set, before H016b's first counted row. Otherwise it can't be the replication for an H016b pass.
- Both tests pass on their own family terms (H016b by Holm in F1, H017 in F2). Both must also pass correct-side cost, with a non-flipping fill-fragility co-report.
- Both passing counts as **one** finding: "REV, forward and historical holdout". It is not two discoveries.
- CASSANDRA gives written sign-off on independence. The concern is the same broker feed or regime overlap.
If any one of these fails, the H016b pass still needs a separate new-ID replication.
orion_rulings.9:
- ORION runs it **once**, from a frozen worktree at the H017 harness tag. This happens only after DATA_CERTIFIED and CASSANDRA_CLEARED exist for that tag.
- The run's start and end times, the commit and the tape digest are logged. Outputs are written sealed.
- Unsealing happens once, with CASSANDRA notified, and the results are recorded as-is. No reruns: a crash before outputs counts as no-run, and any rerun needs CASSANDRA's written approval.
- No waiting for H016b. H016b's kill and futility rules are mechanical and frozen. Stopping H016b early only enters it into Holm at p=1, which is conservative.
orion_rulings.Q2_Q4_Q5_Q8_Q10:
- **Q4: NOT binding.** The pass rule stays P1–P6, mirroring H016b (R1 needs the same decision rule). Making "mean ≥ +0.10R" binding would cut power at a true +0.10 to about a coin flip and add a criterion H016b doesn't have. Instead the mean and its CI are a mandatory co-report. If the mean is below +0.10R, the verdict carries a "small-effect" flag, and MINT may not size above its minimum on it.
- **Q5: KEEP** the pooled N < 400 floor, which gives INCONCLUSIVE (neither PASSES nor FAILS). It applies to the confirmatory pool only.
- **Q8: YES, same rule.** "Same rule" means the pins are byte-identical, including the point constants (min-stop 10.2 / 4.88 pt). Rescaling them to era index levels would be a choice made after knowing the data, so any level-scaled variant needs a new ID. The heavier small-stop gating in low-level eras is a disclosed regime caveat, not a defect.
- **Q2 (advisory):** US500 sub-window B overlaps INV-002's NQ path, so it is exploratory and reported only. The confirmatory pool is US100 plus US500 sub-window A, central N about 653, which is above the Q5 floor. CASSANDRA may overrule.
- **Q10:** I support tagging with pre-declared conditional rules. The window comes from DATA's frozen manifest, and the spread schedule is frozen at harness registration. This means the R3 deadline doesn't hinge on the BID backfill finishing.

replication_deadline.meaning: ORION #6 wording: 'pre-registered, with its tag set, before H016b's first counted row'. In harness-H016b-v1 a 'row' is the sealed log row written by `h016b.py final` (LOG_COLS: computed_at_utc / computed_at_sast are stamped at write time) and the column `counted` is True only for status 'trade' rows with no not-counted reason. So the moment meant is the COMPUTE (write) time of H016b's first row with counted = True - not the start of the session it describes
replication_deadline.earliest_possible: first eligible session = London 2026-10-05 02:00 NY (08:00 SAST). A row for it can only be written once its BID+ASK day files are final, i.e. at >= 2026-10-06 01:00 UTC (03:00 SAST). ORION's runner is scheduled 01:07 UTC Tue-Sat, so the earliest expected counted row is 2026-10-06 ~01:07 UTC = ~03:07 SAST (Tuesday), if London or NY AM of 2026-10-05 yields a counted trade on either instrument; otherwise the first counted row comes on a later run (it can only move later)
replication_deadline.binding_deadline: prereg-H017 must be tagged and visible on origin before 2026-10-06 01:00 UTC (03:00 SAST), the earliest moment any H016b row for a counted session can exist; this needs no reading of H016b's log. If that is missed, it still qualifies iff its tagger time and its logged origin appearance (git ls-remote) both precede computed_at_utc of H016b's first counted = True row, checked afterwards by reading only that row's timestamp and status columns (no R)
replication_deadline.conservative_target: tag before the first counted SESSION starts, 2026-10-05 02:00 NY = 08:00 SAST, so no 'row vs session' dispute can arise
replication_deadline.if_missed: H017 remains a valid stand-alone F2 holdout test (nothing else changes), but it cannot be H016b's replication; an H016b pass would need a separate new-ID replication

cassandra_rulings.Q2:
CASSANDRA ruling Q2: US500 2022-12-27 → 2025-05-30 (sub-window B) is EXPLORATORY and reported only. It is never part of P1–P6, the N floor, the family F2 p-value, or replication eligibility.
The confirmatory pool is US100 2019-02-04 → 2022-12-23 plus US500 2019-02-04 → 2022-12-23 (sub-window A). Both end at the same date.
Reason: INV-002 tested sweep, range and FVG concept families (H001b–H004b, H009b) on Kaggle NQ 1m from 2022-12-26 18:01 ET. US100 tracks NQ at 0.98–0.99 and US500 is strongly correlated, so B's path has been seen. Also, the burned-export and QUANT-canon pipelines loaded the US500 2025.parquet (Jan–May 2025 lies in B) before filtering it out.
cassandra_rulings.Q3:
CASSANDRA ruling Q3: REV is an intraday rule that reads daily context. The only touched HTF file that overlaps is NQ=F *weekly* from 2021-09-13. It is "not primary" in H009b, which used daily 2024-09-13+.
No HERMES analysis of US100/NQ intraday or daily bars before 2022-12-26 was found (see contamination). The US100 end of 2022-12-23 exists because Kaggle NQ starts 2022-12-26 18:01 ET. There is no overlap.
cassandra_rulings.Q4:
CASSANDRA ruling Q4: ORION's premise "mirroring H016b" is factually wrong. harness-H016b-v1 `verdict()` has six criteria, and the first is `mean_R >= 0.10`. H017's P1–P5 therefore set a lower bar than H016b.
- Standalone F2 verdict: P1–P6 as drafted, with the mean and CI co-reported and the small-effect flag as ORION ruled.
- Replication eligibility (ORION #6, R1/R4): H017 counts as H016b's replication, or the reverse, only if its confirmatory pool ALSO meets pooled mean ≥ +0.10R. That makes the decision rule identical to H016b's.
- An H017 PASS with mean < +0.10R is a valid F2 result but NOT a replication.
cassandra_rulings.Q5:
CASSANDRA ruling Q5: Keep the pooled N < 400 → INCONCLUSIVE rule on the confirmatory pool.
An INCONCLUSIVE run still CONSUMES the holdout: no rerun, no extension.
Pre-run check (outcome-free): before the run, DATA counts, from the frozen manifest alone, the eligible killzone sessions that have BID and ASK day files. ORION multiplies that count by the burned per-session trade rates (US100 0.2647, US500 0.2022) and by the draft's level-adjusted keep fractions.
If that expected confirmatory N is < 450, the run is POSTPONED: the holdout stays sealed and unread. Without the 2019-01 → 2020-07-06 BID backfill, the central confirmatory N falls to about 450.
cassandra_rulings.Q8:
CASSANDRA ruling Q8: Same rule, because the pins are byte-identical.
- The min-stop (4 × (assumed spread + 2 × slip)) is friction-relative, not range-relative. Re-deriving it per era would be a different rule and needs a new ID.
- The prereg MUST state before the run, as a pre-data expectation, what my burned-data and public-level estimate shows (scratch `h017_cost_scaling.py`). It assumes the gross edge in R is scale-invariant and uses DATA's published 2022–2025-08 US100 off-RTH spread of about 3.46 pt (burned 1.18).

| | Burned mean R | Implied holdout mean R | Level-scaled keep rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| US100 | +0.006 | **−0.10** | 75–91% |
| US500 | +0.18 | +0.23 | 38–88% |

- P2 (US100 > 0) is therefore the expected binding failure point, for cost reasons alone.
- A FAIL driven by US100 costs is a valid FAIL of the pinned rule. It must not be reworded afterwards as "era costs, not edge".
cassandra_rulings.Q10:
CASSANDRA ruling Q10: Tag with conditional rules, provided each one is mechanical:
(i) The counted start per instrument = the first NYSE full session preceded by 22 sessions with both BID and ASK day files in DATA's frozen manifest. Window ends as Q2/Q3.
(ii) The era spread schedule is frozen at harness registration and used ONLY in co-reports. Binding fills use the measured ASK.
(iii) No choice may be made after any holdout file has been decoded by the harness.
(iv) DATA_CERTIFIED for H017 must cover the Dukascopy BID+ASK bi5 feed for 2019-2022. DATA's §4 currently certifies the range as "HistData BID; no ASK", which is not the feed H017 binds to (Q7).
cassandra_rulings.R5:
CASSANDRA R5 (draft, 2026-10-04): I sign off that H017's confirmatory pool (US100 + US500, 2019-02-04 → 2022-12-23) is independent of H016b's counted window (sessions from 2026-10-05) for ORION #6 purposes, subject to the conditions below.
- **Time and market path:** no session overlap. No HERMES analysis of these instruments' bars in this window was found. US500 sub-window B is excluded for its INV-002 path overlap.
- **Regime:** 2019-2022 (COVID, 2021 melt-up, 2022 bear) is a different regime from 2026. That supports independence, but limits transfer.
- **Constants:** the point constants were derived from 2025-26 data and fixed before H017 data. That is legitimate for a frozen-rule test. It means H017 tests the 2026-calibrated rule at different index levels, not the calibration itself.

**Not independent:**
(i) Same vendor (Dukascopy CFD construction and feed artifacts are shared).
(ii) Same code. Mitigated only by A5.
(iii) Same concept source (ICT).
A joint pass is therefore ONE finding (as ORION ruled), not two.

**Conditions:** this sign-off becomes final only when ALL of these hold:
(1) A1–A5 are in the tagged prereg.
(2) `prereg-H017` is on origin before 2026-10-06 01:00 UTC (R3).
(3) DATA certifies the Dukascopy BID+ASK feed for the confirmatory window, with the F4 reads attested as outcome-free.
(4) The A5 independent scorer agrees with the sealed results.
(5) No holdout bar is decoded by anyone before the single run, except DATA's attested integrity QC.

**Missing today:** (1), (3) and (4).
